# Stage 1 report — foundations

Written on 2026-11-14 by a review session that did not write the code (step 1.25, T-181). For the founder first; the last section is for the technical lead.

## In short

- **The planned building of stage 1 is done.** 26 of the plan's 27 steps have landed, and this review is the 27th. The stage now waits for your check (runbook, sections 6 and 9). It is not called finished until you have checked it.
- **The foundations are sound where it matters most.** Keeping one league's data away from another's is built three times over, is tested on every change, and held when it was tried on the test copy of the database at Supabase on 2026-11-13.
- **It runs only on this computer, on made-up data held in memory.** The website has never run on a real database. Nothing can be put online yet.
- **The review found four large pieces that the stage's exit test needs but that were never in any plan**: the website on a real database, a background worker that actually starts, a way to ship a release and take it back, and the web pages for sending and accepting an invitation. They are proposed as new steps 2.92 to 2.97 below. Your supervised session can only succeed after they land.
- **Your part** is a short list of accounts and settings that only you can make (the checklist at the end), then that one supervised session.

## What now exists

All of this is in the repository, checked automatically on GitHub's machines every time something is pushed.

- **The code is split into parts with fixed rules between them.** Two programs (the website and the background worker) and nine shared libraries. Automatic checks fail the build if a part reaches into another the wrong way, if a league is named in the code, if database commands are written outside the database part, if a league's web address is written by hand, if a secret could reach a visitor's browser, if screen text is typed into a screen instead of the message files, or if a database change would delete or rename something in one step. Each check has a test that plants a mistake and proves the check catches it.
- **Settings are checked once at start-up.** The website refuses to start if a setting is missing or wrong, and names the setting without ever printing its value. `.env.example` lists every setting with made-up values.
- **The database's shape** is written as eleven numbered files (called "migrations") that a runner applies in order. Stage 1 made the tables for accounts, profiles, leagues, programs, seasons, roles, invitations, the activity log, staff visits, command receipts and background jobs; stage 2 has since added divisions, venues, people, teams, rosters, schedules, games, standings and imports.
- **The league fence.** Every league table carries its league, and the database itself hides every row that is not the current league's. The website and worker use a restricted database user that cannot change the database's shape or see past the fence. A test creates two leagues and tries every command and every database query of one against the other's records; any success fails the build. Another test runs every role against every command.
- **Leagues and access.** Creating a league (internal tool), short names with a blocked list and forwarding after a rename, the four league states (draft, live, archived, suspended), seasons, the fixed roles and what each may do, invitations (send, accept, re-send, cancel, expire), removing access at once, and the activity log.
- **Sign-in.** Sign up with an emailed 6-digit code and a password, sign in, forgotten password, a "Continue with Google" button, staying signed in with no time limit, the list of your devices with "sign out everywhere", the password again before sensitive actions, an email when a new device signs in, and limits on wrong guesses. The screens answer the same whether or not an account exists, so they cannot be used to find out who has one. It runs on a local stand-in (a pretend sign-in service inside the program). The adapter for the real service, Supabase (the piece of our code that talks to that service), is written and tested against recorded answers but has never talked to Supabase.
- **The website.** Our own pages, each league's public pages with its own colors, header, menu and footer ("Powered by SR Leagues"), two clearly different starting designs, right-to-left text such as Arabic shown correctly, and the admin area with its ten sections. Someone without access who types an admin address is told "you do not have access"; a league not yet published is hidden from everyone but its staff.
- **The background worker's parts.** A job queue whose jobs are saved together with the change that caused them, the invitation email job, an email sender that keeps every email instead of sending it (so no email leaves the machine outside production), and an adapter for the real email service, Resend, not yet tried against it.
- **Logs and errors.** Structured logs with a request number and no personal details, an error-reporting interface with an adapter for Sentry (not yet tried against it), and health checks.
- **Made-up data.** `npm run seed` loads two made-up leagues (Lakeside Hoops League and Maple Street Rec League, every email ending in `example.test`) into a database on this computer.
- **Browser tests** that drive a real browser: two leagues with different looks, signing in and still being signed in after the browser closes, and a member of staff of the first league refused at every admin address of the second.
- **Records and guides.** Decision records in `docs/architecture/decisions/`, and two guides: [run it locally](../operations/run-it-locally.md) and [apply migrations](../operations/apply-migrations.md).

Much of stage 2 has been built alongside (schedule, standings, statistics and team pages, several admin screens), on the same made-up stand-in.

## See it working on your computer

The quickest way needs no settings file and touches nothing real:

1. Open a terminal in the repository's folder.
2. Run `node scripts/preview-web.mjs`. The first time it takes several minutes: it makes a private copy under `.local/preview`, installs and builds it. Later starts are faster. It answers only this computer.
3. Open `http://127.0.0.1:3210/north-valley` and `http://127.0.0.1:3210/harbor-city`: two made-up leagues, each with its own look. Their schedule, standings, statistics and teams pages show made-up results.
4. Open `http://127.0.0.1:3210/signin` and sign in as the made-up member: email `member@example.test`, password `made-up member password`. Close the browser, open it again and go back: you are still signed in. `/account` shows your devices and "sign out everywhere".
5. Stop it with Ctrl+C in the terminal.

What to know while you look:

- **Nothing is saved.** The leagues and people live in the program's memory and go back to their starting state each time it starts. They are not the two leagues `npm run seed` loads: the website does not read that database yet (finding R1).
- **You cannot sign up with a new email address here.** The code email is kept in memory where nobody can read it (finding R5).
- **The made-up member runs no league,** so the admin pages say "you do not have access". The browser tests reach them as made-up league staff; a simple way for you to do the same is part of step 2.96.
- The guide `docs/operations/run-it-locally.md` describes the developer way (`npm run dev:web`). It asks you to copy `.env.example` to `.env`: **do not do that if you already have a `.env` with the live tracker's settings**, because it would replace them. The preview above needs no `.env`.

## What the review found

Severity: **High** means the stage's exit test cannot pass, or the product cannot go online, until it is fixed. **Medium** means it must be fixed before real people use the product. **Low** is tidying.

**What held up well.** The league fence: every table has its one forced rule, a test fails any new table without one, the league is set for one database transaction only (so a reused connection cannot carry one league into the next request, and a test proves it), and the website checks at start-up that its database user is the restricted one. The sign-in screens went through two security reviews and their findings were fixed. The structure checks each prove they catch a planted mistake. A search of the build branch's history for the shapes of real database addresses and keys found only made-up values. The live tracker's site was not touched: it is still published from one fixed commit.

**R1 — High. The website cannot run on a real database, and no step owns making it do so.** On the test copy or in production it refuses to start, on purpose, until sign-in on Supabase is connected. That cannot be connected because the small database functions promised for steps 1.12 to 1.14 (create an account, find an account by email at sign-in without revealing whether it exists, show the names on a league's list of staff) and the tables the Supabase adapter keeps for itself (devices, sessions, attempt counts) were never built. Meanwhile every stage 2 screen lands "on the stand-in only", with its database part waiting for "when the web app can start on a database" (steps 2.89 and 2.90 say so). The longer this waits, the more there is to connect. **New steps 2.92 and 2.93.**

**R2 — High. The background worker never starts.** Its parts exist, but there is no start-up: it reads no settings, does not check its database user, never starts taking jobs and never reports that it is alive. Outside the tests, an invitation email, an import or anything else left for it would wait forever. **New step 2.94.**

**R3 — High. Nothing can be released or taken back.** The only container image in the repository (a packaged copy of a program that a host such as Render can run) is the live tracker's. There is no image for the website and worker, no release command that applies the database changes first (T-48), no way to go back to the previous version (T-156), and none of the written procedures T8 section 11 asks for (releasing and reversing, restoring the database, changing a secret). Stage 1's exit test says "a release is shipped and then reversed". **New step 2.95.**

**R4 — High. The invitation part of the exit test has no web side.** The email is built, but there is no screen to invite anyone and no page at the address the email links to (`/{league}/invitation/...`), so its link leads nowhere. Step 2.88, which was added to the plan to finish this test, cannot add the page as written: the folders it may touch do not include the pages folder. Stage 2's demo also needs Al-Hadi's staff to have accounts and roles. **New step 2.97;** step 2.88 should then wait for 2.96 and 2.97.

**R5 — Medium. Kept emails cannot be read.** T-140 promises a viewer for the emails that are kept instead of sent; none exists. So a new address cannot finish signing up on this computer, emails on the test copy would be kept where nobody can see them (and the supervised session needs to read one), and only the one made-up member can sign in by hand. **New step 2.96.**

**R6 — Medium. Protections due before real people have accounts are in no step.** The browser is not yet told to run only our own scripts (T-79: today the rule only forbids putting our pages inside another site), and not told to always use HTTPS. There is no bot check in front of sign-in (T4 section 6). The setting that tells the website which visitor a request came from cannot describe Cloudflare in front of Render, the hosting T1 chose: with today's choices, every visitor would look like Cloudflare, so one person's wrong passwords could lock out many. The test that harmful text typed into a field comes out as plain text (T4 section 12) does not exist. The list of offensive short names is empty. This must be done before Al-Hadi's staff get real accounts in stage 2. **New step 2.98.**

**R7 — Medium. Some checks T9 says every change must pass are not in the gate**, though the build order says stage 1 has them running: a scan of the libraries we use for known security holes, a scan for passwords committed by mistake, a scan of the built website's browser files for secrets (today only the source is scanned), a build of the worker, the size limit for a public page (T-161), weekly proposals to update libraries, and a check that nobody writes TypeScript's "anything goes" type `any` (T-32; one test file does). **New step 2.99.**

**R8 — Medium. Two settings traps.** The website and the live tracker both read a setting named `DATABASE_URL`, so a settings file made for one points the other at its database; once the website runs on a database, a settings file made for the tracker could point the website at the live Al-Hadi database. And the website demands two Stripe keys and a "session secret" that nothing uses yet, so the test copy would need Stripe keys years before payments exist. **Fixed as part of step 2.93.**

**R9 — Low. The website's database user may change any part of its own account row, email included,** where T-73 wants an email change confirmed from the new address first. The code does not do it today; the database should not allow it either. **Part of step 2.92.**

**R10 — Low. The parts do not list the libraries they use;** everything is installed once for the whole repository. Harmless today, but the program image of step 2.95 should install only what it needs. **Part of step 2.95.**

**R11 — Low. The specification and records disagree with the code in places (T-185).** T1 names Tailwind and shadcn/ui for styling; neither is used and no record says why. T2 names two folders that do not exist (`supabase/seed`, `tests/integration`) and leaves out the logging library. T4 says the small account functions came with the access and sign-in steps; they did not. T4 and T8 say `main` changes only through pull requests; it moves through the promote script. Record 031 says migration 0011 is reserved for sign-in; it went to a games fix. The stage 1 plan says everything short of the vendor accounts was built and tested locally; R1 to R4 show it was not. The decisions file shows its T4 table three times. There is no record for the logging and error-reporting choices of step 1.20. The note in `postgres-driver.ts` and the apply-migrations guide still say the runner has never run against a hosted database, though it did on 2026-11-13. **New step 2.100** (the last two are fixed in step 2.95, which touches those files).

**Notes for the lead (no step).** The log line of 2026-11-14 for steps 1.27 and 1.22 claimed more about the stage than was true; a later line corrects it. Of the work that needs the test copy, only the migrations and the fence have been tried there; the two-league test, the job queue, sign-in, email and the website itself have not.

## Your checklist

Only you can do these. None of them stops the building meanwhile.

**Now, on your own:**

1. **Turn on two-step sign-in (T-83)** for GitHub, for the email account that all the others recover to, and for Supabase. Then for each new account below as you make it, and for the domain registrar. About twenty minutes each, in each service's own settings.
2. **Set up the shared password vault (T-166)** with emergency access for your trusted second person, and keep every business login in it.
3. **Create the accounts:** Render (hosting for the website and worker), Cloudflare (in front of it), Resend (sending email) and a domain for the product. Also wanted: Sentry (error reports) and an uptime checker. Each has a price: check it before you sign up, because spending is yours to decide (T-167).
4. **For the test copy on Supabase:** put its two API keys into the git-ignored file `.env.staging` (or into the vault for the session), download Supabase's certificate file, and change the database password: the first one was pasted into a chat, so it must be treated as known.
5. **Google sign-in:** make a sign-in key in your Google account when you want Google sign-in tested.
6. **Refusing leaked passwords on Supabase (T-85):** decide whether to switch it on. If it needs a paid plan, it costs money, so it is yours.
7. **Continuous backup (T-153):** it is a paid extra on Supabase. Say yes to its cost; it is switched on in the session below.
8. **Say yes, or name what to change,** to the answers the lead gave for you: `docs/specs/v1/DECISIONS.md`, "Decided for you, waiting for your yes".
9. **Recommended, in GitHub's settings for this repository:** switch on, if they are not on already, its free alerts for libraries with known security holes and its scan for committed passwords, and protect `main` from being force-pushed or deleted (ordinary pushes stay allowed, so the promote script keeps working).

**Then, after steps 2.92 to 2.97 have landed: one supervised session.** You start it; the lead does the technical part with you there. In it: connect the test copy with its keys and certificate, bring it up to the newest migrations, run the two-league test against it, start the website and the worker on Render behind Cloudflare, send yourself an invitation and accept it, switch on continuous backup, ship a release and then take it back, and set the uptime checks. After that you try it, and say whether stage 1 passes.

## For the lead: details of the proposed steps

Each line is ready to go into the stage 2 plan, after 2.91. Reserve numbers at opening as usual. Step 2.100 follows 2.99: `scripts/build-dashboard.mjs` reads a step number as text and splits it into two whole numbers, so it does not clash with step 2.10.

- **2.92 Accounts on the real database.** A migration (0012) with the Supabase adapter's store tables (devices, sessions, attempt counts, codes' proofs: record 018, `packages/providers/src/sign-in/supabase/sign-in-store.ts`) and the owner-run functions record 008 assigned to steps 1.12 to 1.14 and nobody built: create and erase an account with its own profile, find an account by email for sign-in without saying whether it exists (T-68), and the display names on the access list of the league that is set (`list-access.ts` says "not built yet"). Decide in a record how a Supabase user id becomes an account id (Supabase ids are not UUID version 7, T-41). Narrow `grant update on public.accounts` to the columns the app may change, with email only through T-73's confirmed change (R9). Each function goes into the reviewed list in `app-role.test.ts`. _Spec: T4 §2 and §3, T-221, T-230, records 008 and 018. Needs: nothing new. Migration: yes. Folders: `supabase/migrations`, `packages/database`, `packages/providers/src/sign-in/supabase`. Done test: the production store passes `memory-sign-in-store.test.ts`'s cases on PGlite; each function is in the reviewed list; the two-league harness covers the new queries. Model: opus, high._
- **2.93 The website on the real database.** Database-backed `WebPorts` in `apps/web/src/server/container.ts`: local mode may use the seeded PGlite database (so the preview shows the seed leagues), staging and production use PostgreSQL with the Supabase adapter and 2.92's store, `startup.ts` stops refusing staging once wired, and the health check asks the database. Then each stand-in-only area moves over in its own part: public schedule, standings and statistics, teams, Admin → Teams, the schedule grid, fixture import, the games area, the tracker (2.89 and 2.90 then drop their database halves). Also R8: rename the web app's `DATABASE_URL` (for example `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`) so it can never pick up the tracker's, and make `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `SESSION_SECRET` required only once something uses them; update `.env.example`, `run-it-locally.md` and the `.env.example` test. _Spec: T2 §4, T-30, T-60, T-232. Needs: 2.92. Migration: no. Model: opus, high. Built in parts._

Needs: nothing new. Migration: maybe (pg-boss tables). Model: opus._
- **2.95 One image, a release and its reversal.** One container image for web and worker (T1 §1), each workspace declaring its own dependencies (R10); a release command that runs `applyMigrations` with the migration login and only then starts the new version (T-48, T-49); reversing to the previous image (T-156); the Render services written down (blueprint file or checklist), Cloudflare in front; `docs/operations/` procedures for releasing and reversing, restoring the database, and rotating a secret (T8 §11, T-165: each counts as written once followed in the supervised session); correct the hosted-database notes in `postgres-driver.ts` and `apply-migrations.md`.
